title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
hints: for a rectangle whose height equals bar i's height, how far left and right can it extend? exactly until it hits a bar shorter than heights[i] on each side - so every bar's best possible rectangle is bounded by its nearest shorter bar on the left and right

if you scan left to right keeping a stack of indices with increasing heights, then whenever the current bar is shorter than the stack's top, the top bar has just found its right boundary (the current index) - and once popped, whatever is left on the stack is its left boundary
when you pop index i because the current bar is shorter, compute width as (current index - new stack top index - 1), or just current index if the stack is now empty, and area as heights[i] * width
process a final sentinel of height 0 after the last bar (conceptually) to flush out and resolve every remaining bar still on the stack
commonMistakes: computing width incorrectly after popping, forgetting to subtract the new stack top's index minus one, or mishandling the empty-stack case
not flushing the stack at the end, missing rectangles anchored by bars that were never shorter than something later
using a strict comparison inconsistently, causing equal-height bars to be handled incorrectly and undercounting width

content.problemStatement:
You're given a list of non-negative integers representing the heights of
bars in a histogram, where each bar has width 1 and the bars stand side
by side in order.

**Find the area of the largest rectangle that can be formed using one
or more contiguous bars, where the rectangle's height is limited by the
shortest bar it spans, and return that maximum area.**
notes: all bars the same height (the whole histogram is one big rectangle)
strictly increasing or strictly decreasing heights
a height of 0 somewhere in the middle, splitting the histogram

sampleTestCases.explanation: the rectangle formed by the two bars of height 5 and 6 (indices 2-3) has width 2 and height 5, giving area 10, which is the maximum
the single bar of height 4 alone gives area 4, larger than both bars together at height 2 (area 4 as well, tied but not exceeded)
both bars together form a rectangle of width 2 and height 1, area 2

bruteForce.approach: for every pair of start and end bars, find the minimum height between them and compute width times that minimum, tracking the maximum over all pairs
